# Order Status Communications Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Order Status Communications Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 18 captured build checkpoints; 4 skills; 2 knowledge files; 7 acceptance checks; 4 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm licensing for your tenant and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness. Building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved order-communication environment, publisher prefix and maker access. Confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model is available; keep the workshop synthetic and Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded order files, proposed order, carrier and CRM sources, communication channels and the intended channel; document blocked paths rather than bypass them. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always authentication trigger. Record who may build, test and later use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for ERP and MES status data, carrier tracking, CRM and preference data, and the email, EDI, portal and Teams channels. No customer connection is needed for the synthetic workshop. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare service, account, operations and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview, not publication. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: the Copilot Studio browser and reviewed files, with no PAC CLI or YAML import. Easy mode: VS Code Agent mode, the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and a supported PAC CLI. | Customer or partner |
| Communication rule ownership | Have account owners approve draft wording, tiers, preferred channels and approval routes before customer data is used. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Customer service business owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Effort to assemble order, production, shipment, delay and account evidence into an approved customer update. Establish current communication effort and consistency before crediting any change to the agent.

Fill your baseline record:

| Order | Measurement period | Systems consulted | Inquiry received | Update approved | Commitment changes | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree order-communication replacement connections, governance, support, telemetry and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Customer service business owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Customer service business owner | Approve order-communication sources, scope and the approval workflow; agree production success measures without treating synthetic orders as results. |
| Authorized communication reviewers and senders | Approve each customer draft and send it only through an approved channel. |
| Production and logistics validators | Validate production progress, delay causes, recovery actions and carrier milestones before a draft is used. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and four skills; remove web search, confirm the model and keep the owned agent in Draft. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm tenant licensing and capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any order or CRM connection is approved. |
| Order and CRM connection owners | Approve dedicated references for order, production, carrier, CRM and communication sources; own connection failures. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check OS-01 through OS-04 and the boundary tests on the current Draft; fail any claim that an order changed or a message was sent. |
| Operations owner | Own production support, session and credit monitoring and configuration recovery; route commitments to authorized senders. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Order-communication replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures have named agreement.
- [ ] The service owner records how order, production, shipment, delay and account evidence is assembled today before choosing measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/order-status-communication/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The target environment and publisher prefix are approved before any build lane starts.
- [ ] The customer confirms authenticated audience and least-privilege access to order values and customer contact data.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/order-status-communication/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/order-status-communication/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/order-status-communication/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/order-status-communication/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Order Status Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: aibast_order-status-communication-review-rules.md
7. Add knowledge: aibast_order-status-communication-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: aibast_customer_update
9. Add skill: aibast_delay_notification
10. Add skill: aibast_order_lookup
11. Add skill: aibast_shipment_tracking
12. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
13. Open a fresh Preview conversation
14. Pass OS-01: Customer Service Representative
15. Pass OS-02: Account Manager
16. Pass OS-03: Operations Leader
17. Pass OS-04: Account Manager
18. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: OS-01, OS-02, OS-03, OS-04. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, environment, model, inventory, cases and Draft state.
- [ ] If this lane is chosen, the recipe smoke test calls `OrderStatusCommunicationAgent` and returns its required markers.
- [ ] The optional Brainstem lane is recorded as used or skipped; no workshop step depends on it.
- [ ] The manual build has reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, four skills and the confirmed model; web search and tools are absent.
- [ ] Each unchanged order prompt passes once in a separate fresh Preview conversation on the owned Draft.
- [ ] The deterministic validator judges each full response; annotated screenshots do not replace the machine gate.
- [ ] Any Easy/Manual comparison uses identical instructions, knowledge, skills, model and case identifiers.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before showing order values or customer contact details. Request only read scopes for approved order, carrier and CRM data. Restrict the audience and verify access with authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management and MES

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Order and CRM connection owners

1. **Bind Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management and MES — read:** Bind approved read-only connector or API actions.

2. **Identity for Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management and MES:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management and MES:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management and MES:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Change no schedule or order; prepare the internal delay review only. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a live status, record change or sent update.

### Step 3-2. Integrate Approved carrier and logistics tracking

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Order and CRM connection owners

1. **Bind Approved carrier and logistics tracking — read:** Bind least-privilege read-only tracking actions.

2. **Identity for Approved carrier and logistics tracking:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved carrier and logistics tracking:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved carrier and logistics tracking:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 5](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Imply no live access; report the fixed synthetic shipment record. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Return a draft or review and name the approval needed; execute nothing.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Dynamics 365 Customer Service

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Order and CRM connection owners

1. **Bind Dynamics 365 Customer Service — read:** Bind scoped read-only connector actions.

2. **Identity for Dynamics 365 Customer Service:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Dynamics 365 Customer Service:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Dynamics 365 Customer Service:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 7](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Send no Teams message; an approved communication tool and authorized sender are required. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a live status, record change or sent update.

### Step 3-4. Integrate Power Automate and approved communication channels

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Order and CRM connection owners

1. **Bind Power Automate and approved communication channels — write:** Keep drafts unsent; gate sending behind an approval flow and authorized sender (preview).

2. **Identity for Power Automate and approved communication channels:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Power Automate and approved communication channels:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Power Automate and approved communication channels:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 7](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Send no Teams message; an approved communication tool and authorized sender are required. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Return a draft or review and name the approval needed; execute nothing.

### Step 3-5. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Order and CRM connection owners

Create read tools with dedicated references for approved order, production, carrier, logistics, CRM and preference data.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Order, production, carrier, logistics, CRM, communication and collaboration sources use dedicated, verified connection references.
- [ ] Approval and action tools for order, schedule, shipment, recovery or communication changes stay unavailable until explicitly authorized.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Before rollout, test an approved test deployment as service, account and operations users and an unshared identity; maker access does not prove user access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The business owner sets customer-data measures; synthetic dates, values and statuses are not production thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations record the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked order corpus | All four cases, OS-01 through OS-04, satisfy every required and forbidden marker. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, four skills and the reviewed model; no tools or web search. |
| Draft-only boundary | Any claim that an order, schedule, shipment, recovery plan or customer communication was changed or sent is no-go. |
| Visual checkpoint acceptance | Require a positive target-state anchor without a blocker or refusal; withhold reshoot-required images. |
| Release state | The owned workshop agent is Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Customer service business owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Customer service business owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The production publish operation has explicit human confirmation.
- [ ] The approved service audience and supported channels are tested before publication is confirmed.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review failed order sessions, their transcripts, tool connection and authentication errors, and credit use in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the reviewed workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses a restore path supported for the environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, source usage, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.
